title.en: Tell a story with a twist

es: Escribir un relato con un hábito pasado, una deducción, una cláusula de participio, un arrepentimiento con wish y un giro final.

teaching.en: When I was nine, we would visit my grandmother every Sunday.
teaching.es: Cuando tenía nueve años, visitábamos a mi abuela cada domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base cuenta un hábito pasado y crea el escenario del relato.
segments: When I was nine, we would
teaching.audioText: When I was nine, we would visit my grandmother every Sunday.

teaching.en: One evening the cake had disappeared, so the dog must have eaten it.
teaching.es: Una tarde el pastel había desaparecido, así que el perro debió de comérselo.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio da el hecho anterior y must have + participio, la deducción del misterio.
segments: One evening the cake had disappeared, so
the dog must have eaten it.
teaching.audioText: One evening the cake had disappeared, so the dog must have eaten it.

teaching.en: Walking into the kitchen, I noticed a strange smell.
teaching.es: Al entrar en la cocina, noté un olor extraño.
teaching.explanationEs: Verbo + -ing al inicio une dos acciones de la misma persona: quien camina es quien nota.
teaching.audioText: Walking into the kitchen, I noticed a strange smell.

teaching.en: I wish I had locked the door that night.
teaching.es: Ojalá hubiera cerrado con llave la puerta aquella noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + had + participio expresa arrepentimiento por algo pasado.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had locked the door that night.

teaching.en: The twist was that the thief turned out to be my own cousin.
teaching.es: El giro fue que el ladrón resultó ser mi propio primo.
teaching.explanationEs: Turn out to be marca el descubrimiento final que cambia la historia.
segments: The twist was that the thief turned
out to be my own cousin.
teaching.audioText: The twist was that the thief turned out to be my own cousin.

teaching.en: Having eaten the cake, he looked very guilty.
teaching.es: Después de comerse el pastel, parecía muy culpable.
teaching.explanationEs: Having + participio marca una acción terminada antes de la principal.
teaching.audioText: Having eaten the cake, he looked very guilty.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada verano pasábamos una semana en el pueblo de mi tío.»

answer.text: Every summer we would spend a week in my uncle's village
accepted: Every summer we would spend a week in my uncle's village
We would spend a week in my uncle's village every summer

feedback.es: Would + verbo base cuenta un hábito que se repetía en el pasado.

hint.es: Empieza por la expresión de tiempo y usa el modal de los hábitos pasados.

prompt.es: Deduce qué pasó con la ventana.

choices.text: Someone should have left the window open.
Someone must have left the window open.
Someone would leave the window open.

feedback.es: Must have + participio deduce un hecho pasado a partir de una prueba: el suelo mojado.

hint.es: Hay una prueba y una conclusión segura: ¿qué modal deduce el pasado?

origin.text: El suelo está mojado junto a la ventana. Estás seguro de que alguien la dejó abierta.

prompt.es: Completa: «Caminando por la playa, encontré una botella vieja.»

feedback.es: Un verbo en -ing al inicio une dos acciones hechas por la misma persona.

hint.es: Una sola persona hace las dos acciones: acorta la primera con una forma en -ing.

origin.text: ___ along the beach, I found an old bottle.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa un arrepentimiento dentro del relato?

choices.text: I wish I locked my bike.
I hope I had locked my bike.
I wish I had locked my bike.

feedback.es: Wish + had + participio lamenta algo pasado; hope no sirve para lamentar y wish + pasado simple habla de hoy.

origin.text: Dejaste la bici sin candado y te la robaron. Ahora lo lamentas.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en el relato.

Opening the box, I found a letter.

pairs: The twist was that nobody had called.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: escenario, deducción, dos acciones en una y giro.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase de giro para el relato.

answer.text: It turned out that the thief was my neighbour.
accepted: It turned out that the thief was my neighbour.
The twist was that the thief was my neighbour.
The thief turned out to be my neighbour.
It turned out that the thief was my neighbor.
The twist was that the thief was my neighbor.
The thief turned out to be my neighbor.

feedback.es: El giro se cuenta con it turned out that o the twist was that, más el dato inesperado.

origin.text: Giro: la persona que robó la bici resultó ser el vecino.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué critica la narradora.

choices.text: Mia did not ask anyone for help.

feedback.es: She should have called a friend critica que no pidió ayuda cuando oyó los pasos.

origin.audio: Walking home in the dark, Mia heard steps behind her. She should have called a friend.

prompt.es: Corrige la frase del recuadro: ¿cuál usa bien el participio inicial?

choices.text: Walking home, the rain felt cold to me.
Walking home, I felt the first drops of rain.
Walking home, the rain was heavy.

feedback.es: El sujeto de la frase principal debe ser quien hace la acción del participio: I felt, no the rain felt.
Para lamentar algo pasado, wish lleva had + participio.

prompt.es: Escribe tu relato con giro (55–120 palabras) con estos datos.

answer.text: When I was a child, we would spend every summer at my grandparents' farm. One night, the cake had disappeared, so the cat must have eaten it. Walking into the kitchen, I noticed a strange smell. I wish I had locked the door! The twist was that my cousin was the thief. He had eaten the cake and blamed the cat. Everyone laughed, and he promised never to do it again.
accepted: When I was a child, we would spend every summer at my grandparents' farm. One night, the cake had disappeared, so the cat must have eaten it. Walking into the kitchen, I noticed a strange smell. I wish I had locked the door! The twist was that my cousin was the thief. He had eaten the cake and blamed the cat. Everyone laughed, and he promised never to do it again.

When I was little, we used to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm. One night, the cake had disappeared, so the cat must have taken it. Entering the kitchen, I noticed a strange smell. I wish I had locked the door. It turned out that my cousin was the thief. He had eaten the cake and blamed the cat. Everyone laughed, and he promised never to do it again.

feedback.es: El relato necesita escenario, deducción, participio, arrepentimiento y giro, con el pasado bien controlado.

origin.text: Datos: de niño, cada verano ibas a la granja de tus abuelos y jugabas con tu primo (hábito). Una noche desapareció el pastel y dedujiste que fue el gato. Al entrar en la cocina notaste un olor extraño. Te arrepientes de no haber cerrado la puerta. Giro: el culpable era tu primo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase une dos acciones con un participio?

choices.text: Opened the door, I saw a tall man.
To open the door, I saw a tall man.
Opening the door, I saw a tall man.

feedback.es: El participio inicial une dos acciones de la misma persona: Opening… I saw. Las otras formas no son correctas.

origin.text: Abriste la puerta y viste a un hombre alto. Quieres contarlo en una sola frase.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuando era pequeña, veíamos películas cada sábado por la mañana.»

answer.text: When I was little we would watch films every Saturday morning
accepted: When I was little we would watch films every Saturday morning
We would watch films every Saturday morning when I was little

feedback.es: La frase abre con when + pasado simple y cuenta la costumbre con would + verbo base.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se descubre al final.

choices.text: The letter was lost in the post.
The letter was read by the wrong person.

feedback.es: Had never been sent y must have forgotten dan el giro: la carta nunca salió de casa.

origin.audio: It turned out that the letter had never been sent. Someone must have forgotten to post it.
